Compute temperature percentile thresholds for each day of year

Source: R/temperature.R
calculate_percentiles.Rd

Uses a rolling window (in days) over the reference period, followed by a group-by-day-of-year percentile. Matches the CLIMDEX / ACI methodology (see ACI (2018), Appendix A of Garrido et al.): the threshold for a given calendar day is the n-th percentile of the daily TX/TN values falling within a window of window_days days (default 5, i.e. \(\pm\)2 days) around that calendar day, pooled across all years of the reference period.

Usage

calculate_percentiles(daily_dataset, n, reference_period, window_days = 5L)

Arguments

daily_dataset

List with data [lon x lat x days] and daily time, as returned by temp_extremum() – i.e. the daily TX (for T90) or TN (for T10) series, not the raw hourly dataset.

n

Percentile (e.g. 90 or 10).

reference_period

Character vector c("YYYY-MM-DD", "YYYY-MM-DD").

window_days

Width, in days, of the window used to pool neighbouring calendar days before taking the percentile (e.g. 5 pools \(\pm\)2 days around each calendar day). Default 5L, matching the standard CLIMDEX/ACI convention.

Value

A numeric array [lon x lat x 366] (day-of-year 1-366).

Details

Bug fix #1 (see NEWS): earlier versions of this function computed the rolling window/percentile on hourly t2m values (with window_size expressed in hours: 80 for day, 40 for night), then compared the resulting threshold to a daily extremum in .crossing_frequency(). Since the daily max (or min) of ~16 (or 8) hourly values almost always exceeds (or falls below) the 90th (or 10th) percentile of the marginal hourly distribution, this made the exceedance frequency during the reference period itself massively higher than the intended ~10 the reference frequency approximately by construction. calculate_percentiles() now takes the already-reduced daily extremum series (the output of temp_extremum()) as input, so the threshold and the tested variable are computed from the same daily quantity.

Bug fix #2 (see NEWS): even after bug fix #1, the threshold was still computed as a percentile of rolling percentiles: a window_days-wide rolling n-th percentile was first applied along the daily series, and a second n-th percentile was then taken of those already-extreme rolled values, grouped by day-of-year across reference years. This two-stage procedure is systematically biased: taking the n-th percentile of a set of local n-th percentiles pushes the final threshold further into the tail than a single, direct percentile would, so it under-counts the true exceedance frequency (observed ~5.6 even with bug fix #1 alone applied). The standard CLIMDEX/ACI methodology instead pools the raw daily values that fall within window_days of a given calendar day, across all years of the reference period, into a single sample, and takes one percentile of that pooled sample. calculate_percentiles() now follows this pooling approach (no more rolling window / zoo dependency for this function), which empirically recovers the intended ~10
